---
title: "Check Before Release"
subtitle: "A short review that catches almost every embarrassing mistake"
---

::: {.objectives}
**In this chapter**

- Find leftover template text and placeholder settings
- Review a course for accessibility in ten minutes
- Test the course on a small screen and in dark mode
- Recognise the legal and privacy questions to settle before going public
- Get one other person to test it
:::

Once a course is public, learners will find every typo, broken link and leftover
"Placeholder" for you. A structured check before release costs an hour and saves
the awkward emails. Work through the sections below in order.

## 1. Content

1. **Every chapter has objectives at the top**, and every objective is covered by
   at least one question.
2. **Read each chapter once, aloud or slowly.** You will hear what you cannot see:
   sentences that are too long, steps out of order.
3. **Run the spell checker.** In RStudio, open a chapter and press *F7* (or use
   *Edit → Check Spelling*). Do it for every file.
4. **Check facts, numbers and dates**, especially anything that might have changed
   since you wrote it.
5. **Click every link** to an outside website. Web addresses go out of date.

## 2. Leftover template text

The commonest slip is publishing the template's own words. Use RStudio's search
across all files: *Edit → Find in Files…* (*Ctrl+Shift+F*, or *Cmd+Shift+F* on a
Mac). Search for each of these, and fix every hit outside the parts of the course
that you deliberately kept:

- `Course Template`
- `example.org`
- `Placeholder`
- `Your name`
- `placeholder.svg`

Then open `_quarto.yml` and check the lines marked `CHANGE`: the course title, the
description, the web address (`site-url`), the chapter list and the footer.
Also check `index.qmd`: the author line and the date.

## 3. The look

Render the whole website with **Render Website**, not just a single file, so no
stale pages remain. Then look at it the way learners will:

- **On a small screen.** Make the browser window narrow (drag its edge) until the
  layout switches to the phone view. Text should stay readable, and no
  horizontal scrolling should be needed. Better still, open the published site on
  a real phone once.
- **In dark mode.** Switch your computer to dark appearance and reload. Text,
  boxes and the logo should stay legible.
- **In the print preview**, if learners will print chapters.
- **In the search.** Type a word you know is in a chapter, and confirm it is
  found. Search works on the published site, and may not when you open the files
  from disk.

## 4. Accessibility

A course that not everyone can use is unfinished. Ten minutes:

1. **Alt text** on every image (Chapter 4). No "image1".
2. **Headings** in order, never skipped, never faked with bold text (Chapter 3).
3. **Link text** that makes sense alone. Search your chapters for "click here".
4. **No information by colour alone.** If a sentence says "the red button", add a
   name.
5. **Video has captions or a transcript.**
6. **Try the keyboard.** Press *Tab* repeatedly through a page and check that you
   can reach and use links, menus and the quiz buttons without a mouse.

The standard behind these points is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
[@w3c2023wcag22]; the template's colours already pass its contrast requirements,
so you only need to keep to the habits above.

## 5. Legal and privacy

::: {.callout-important}
## Ask, do not guess

The rules for what a public university website must contain, and what may be
published, are set by your institution. Confirm the following with the responsible
office before release.
:::

- **Imprint and privacy notice.** Public websites in Germany normally need an
  imprint (*Impressum*) and, where personal data is processed, a privacy notice.
  Ask your communications or data-protection office for the standard wording and
  the address to link to. The footer in `_quarto.yml` has a commented-out example
  showing where such a link goes.
- **Picture, text and video rights.** Do you have the right to publish every image,
  table and quotation? Is each one credited as its licence requires?
- **Patient and personal data.** Nothing that identifies a patient or a colleague,
  in text, images, screenshots or file names. Look at screenshots for name fields,
  record numbers and dates of birth.
- **Third-party services.** If you have embedded a video or map from an outside
  provider, your data-protection office needs to have approved it.
- **The licence of your own material.** State how others may reuse the course, if
  at all, in the footer or on the landing page.

## 6. A fresh pair of eyes

Ask one person who does not know the subject to work through one chapter while you
watch, and say nothing. Note every place they hesitate, re-read or click the wrong
thing. These are the places to improve. You will learn more in twenty minutes than
in a day of rereading your own text.

## 7. Before you press publish

- The whole website has been rendered again after your last change.
- Nothing is left in the sidebar that you do not want learners to see. Drafts start
  with an underscore.
- You know what web address the course will have, and it is entered as `site-url`.

You are ready for Chapter 8.

## Check your understanding

::: {.quiz-score}
:::

::: {.question}
Which of these is the best way to find leftover placeholder text across the whole project?

- [ ] Read every chapter again
- [x] Use *Edit → Find in Files* and search for the placeholder words
- [ ] Ask a learner to report them
- [ ] Render the website and look at the sidebar

::: {.feedback}
A search across all files finds every hit in seconds, including ones in files you
have not opened for weeks. Reading is slower and easily misses things.
:::
:::

::: {.question}
A screenshot in your chapter shows the RStudio window on your own computer, including a project name and your user name. What should you do?

- [ ] Nothing; a screenshot is not personal data
- [x] Check it for anything that identifies a person or a patient, and crop or redo it if necessary
- [ ] Add alt text and move on
- [ ] Reduce its size

::: {.feedback}
Screenshots regularly reveal names, file paths and records that their authors did
not notice. Look at the whole picture, at full size, before publishing.
:::
:::

::: {.question}
Why render the *whole* website before release, rather than only the chapter you last changed?

- [ ] It is faster
- [ ] Single pages cannot be published
- [x] A full render rebuilds every page and clears out pages that no longer belong to the course
- [ ] It creates the search box

::: {.feedback}
A full render leaves the output folder in the exact state that will be published,
with no stale leftovers from earlier versions.
:::
:::

The menu you use in RStudio to search through every file at once is called *Edit → Find in [?]{.fitb answer="Files"}*.
